summary: Official reward programmes outside the US are few and publish little. South Korea's ACRC is the only one with sizeable sums: 36.53 billion won in corruption rewards over 2010-2025 against 417.14 billion recovered, plus public-interest and public-funds rewards, and a switch to a flat 30% with no cap from 29 Sep 2026; but only cumulative totals and two single years were found. Ontario's securities regulator announces individual awards (about CAD 10 million+ in total since 2016); Canada's CRA offshore informant programme is still open but has only second-hand figures; UK HMRC informant payments are known only from FOI press reports (under £1 million a year), and a new US-style Strengthened Reward Scheme was announced in Nov 2025 after a decade of the UK rejecting rewards (FCA/PRA 2014). Ghana, Taiwan, Slovakia and Lithuania have reward laws with tiny or no reported payouts.

programs.name: ACRC rewards for corruption, public-interest and public-funds fraud reports (보상금)
programs.notes: Run by the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (ACRC). Three laws: the ACRC Act (corruption in the public sector; rewards since at least 2002 under its predecessor law), the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Act (private-sector violations, in force 30 Sep 2011) and the Public Funds Recovery Act (fraudulent claims for public money). A reward (보상금) is paid on application when a report directly recovers or increases public revenue; a separate monetary award (포상금) can be paid for public benefit without a recovery. Until Sep 2026: 4-30% sliding scale, cap 3 billion KRW (removed for public-interest reports in Aug 2024). From 29 Sep 2026: flat 30% with no cap (media report). The ACRC publishes cumulative totals in its annual report and quarterly payment announcements; a year-by-year series was not found. Launch year of corruption rewards not confirmed in a document read.

programs.name: Ontario Securities Commission Whistleblower Program (OSC Policy 15-601)
programs.notes: Ontario's securities regulator pays 5-15% of monetary sanctions and voluntary payments of at least CAD 1 million, up to CAD 5 million; up to CAD 1.5 million is paid even if the OSC does not collect. Awards are discretionary; anonymous filing through a lawyer. The OSC announces individual awards by news release and gives cumulative totals; no annual statistics report.

programs.name: Canada Revenue Agency Offshore Tax Informant Program (OTIP)
programs.notes: CRA signs contracts with informants who report major international tax evasion or aggressive avoidance; if at least CAD 100,000 of federal tax is collected (excluding penalties and interest), the informant may get 5-15% of it (tiers of 2.5 points). Rewards are taxable. Pages modified 2026-08-11 show it still open (not closed). CRA does not publish regular statistics; figures come from an ATIP request (2019) and a CRA official's talk (2020). Launch (reportedly January 2014) not confirmed in a document read.

programs.name: HMRC payments to informants (discretionary rewards)
programs.notes: HM Revenue & Customs has long made small discretionary payments to informants out of its Risk and Intelligence Service budget, under section 26 of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005 (per Civil Service World 2019). No published rules or rates; yearly totals are known only from FOI requests reported in the press (about £156,000 in 2007/08 to about £978,000 in 2023/24). Superseded for large cases by the Strengthened Reward Scheme (gbr-hmrc-srs) announced in Nov 2025.

programs.name: HMRC Strengthened Reward Scheme
programs.notes: Announced at the 26 Nov 2025 Budget. 15-30% of tax collected (excluding penalties and interest) when information leads to collection of at least £1.5 million; discretionary; anonymous reports are not paid. Advocacy sources say it applies from 6 April 2026 (not confirmed in an official document read). launched = guidance publication date.

programs.name: Taiwan Ministry of Justice rewards for reporting corruption (獎勵保護檢舉貪污瀆職辦法)
programs.notes: Rewards for reporting corruption and malfeasance by officials, paid when a court convicts: one third after a first conviction, the rest when final. Amounts follow a schedule by sentence, not a share of money recovered (unlike most programmes here); +50% if more than five offenders convicted, max NT$10 million per case. No reward for anonymous reports. The Agency Against Corruption publishes yearly reward statistics (data.gov.tw dataset 134551), but its site could not be reached from here.

programs.name: Ghana Whistleblower Reward Fund (Whistleblower Act 2006, Act 720)
programs.notes: Act 720 creates a Whistleblower Reward Fund financed by voluntary contributions and money voted by Parliament; a disclosure that leads to recovery earns 10% of the money recovered or an amount set by the Attorney-General with the Inspector-General of Police; rewards also on conviction. In Dec 2022 the Attorney-General said Cabinet approved an amendment to operationalise the Fund, implying it had not worked. No figures on payments found. launched = date of assent.

programs.name: Slovakia Whistleblower Protection Office rewards (Act No. 54/2019)
programs.notes: The Whistleblower Protection Office (Úrad na ochranu oznamovateľov) may grant a reward of up to 50 times the minimum wage for a qualified report once an indictment is filed or an administrative offence is finally decided; the reward is not a legal entitlement and depends on merit, lost earnings and assets protected or recovered. Fixed cap, not a share of money recovered. Annual reports 2021-2025 show 7 requests in total and no reward granted (2 still pending at end-2025). Before 2021 the Ministry of Justice handled rewards under Act 307/2014 (not researched). launched = Office's first reward requests (Sept 2021).

programs.name: Lithuania rewards for valuable information (Law on the Protection of Whistleblowers, Art. 12)
programs.notes: Under the Law on the Protection of Whistleblowers (XIII-804, in force 2019), the Prosecutor General's Office, as competent authority, may pay a reward for valuable information (Art. 12 'Atlyginimas pranešėjams už vertingą informaciją'). 2019-2022: 11 requests, 4 granted, 34,000 EUR (from the Office's activity reports, via Transparency International Lithuania). Reward rate and cap not read (the e-seimas page loads the article text dynamically).

programs.name: EU Whistleblower Directive (Directive (EU) 2019/1937)
programs.notes: European Union. Minimum standards for protecting people who report breaches of EU law (reporting channels, protection against retaliation); no financial rewards. Transposition deadline 17 Dec 2021. Context for why EU countries rarely pay rewards. Jurisdiction INTL = European Union.

Korea: the 2015 annual report's '209 cases' for 2008-2015 is hard to square with 113 cases in 2017 alone; possibly a different count. Not resolved.

Canada OSC: no annual tips or awards series after March 2022; whether any awards were announced in 2025-2026 not checked (OSC news search loads by script). OSC Policy 15-601 text itself not downloaded (rules taken from OSC web pages).

Canada CRA OTIP: no official statistics; canada.ca refused scripted downloads, so CRA pages were read through WebFetch and not stored. Launch date (Jan 2014) not confirmed in a document read. The brief's suggestion that OTIP closed is not borne out: pages modified 2026-08-11 still describe an open programme.

UK HMRC: no official publication of informant payments; all yearly totals are press reports of FOI responses (2007/08, 2009/10-2011/12, 2013, 2017/18, 2023/24, 2024/25). Missing years 2008/09-2010/11 individually, 2012/13-2016/17, 2018/19-2022/23. The original FOI responses (e.g. on WhatDoTheyKnow or gov.uk FOI releases) not found.
